requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: The fix makes the type collector avoid indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` in two diagnostic paths: BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and MemberNeedsKey. It also wraps the analyzer's report callback so it silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree in the current compilation. Three new tests compile a library to a metadata-only image. They then check two things: the analyzer/generator run produces no diagnostics, and the expected resolver hint name is generated. The change also edits README, MsgPack004 docs and, unrelatedly, the runtime `MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer<T>`.
story.why: Members of a generic value type from metadata have no syntax, so `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` throws. That made the generator and analyzer fail and the resolver silently disappear (REQ-2283).
touches_beyond_requirement: src/MessagePack/MessagePackSecurity.cs: string keys now bypass the hash-collision-resistant comparer even when HashCollisionResistant is on (runtime, untrusted-data path)
Report wrapper drops every analyzer diagnostic without an in-compilation source location, including Location.None diagnostics for the project's own types
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md document a new 'reported by the defining assembly' policy
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The two changed indexing sites are clearly safe now. The tests use the issue's own repro shape and check that the resolver is generated. I cannot see whether the third site named in the issue (old line ~735) was reached or fixed. I also cannot confirm the VerifyCS harness runs MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer. The MessagePackSecurity edit is unrelated and weakens a security default; the static check S6 did not flag it.

findings.description: Claim C1 disputed: The requirement quote cites three DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] crash sites inside GetObjectInfo (old lines 735, 1009, 1101), and the 24-line offset in the diff (1009 -> 985, 1101 -> 1077) shows only two of those three sites were updated in TypeCollector.cs, leaving the first site (~line 711) untouched. In addition, line 985 only updates the IPropertySymbol path via GetPropertyIdentifierLocation (not any field path), and no test exercises BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull on a metadata symbol.

Claim C5 disputed: ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference does not use the issue's exact app source or project build: GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 575-576 append an explicit [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { } instead of testing the issue's implicit assembly-level GeneratedMessagePackResolver generation, and CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync (lines 661-674) compiles lib without running MessagePackGenerator on it.

Claim C6 disputed: The claim's substance is right, but its citation (GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 637-648) only covers the first VerifyCS.Test check and omits lines 651-658 where the second generator-only CSharpGeneratorDriver check actually appears.

Under UntrustedData / HashCollisionResistant, string keys now use the default comparer. The comment claims string hashing is randomized per process, but that is not true on .NET Framework (netstandard2.0 consumers) unless explicitly configured. This silently removes hash-flooding protection for string-keyed dictionaries deserialized from untrusted input. Unrelated to REQ-2283.

The wrapper drops every diagnostic whose Location is not in source, including Location.None. Any existing diagnostic for the project's own types that falls back to a null location (for example when a GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation helper returns null) is now silently suppressed rather than reported. This is a broad change to analyzer output, not limited to metadata types.

The issue names three direct `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). The diff changes only two hunks (old ~984 and ~1076). The visible diff does not show whether the third site was already safe, was this one, or remains unfixed.

GetEqualityComparer<T>() unconditionally returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default for string without a #if NET / #if NETCOREAPP guard, assuming string.GetHashCode() is always randomized per process. On .NET Framework (used via netstandard2.0/net472 builds), string.GetHashCode() is deterministic by default unless UseRandomizedStringHashAlgorithm is enabled in app.config, so this silently disables MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData (HashCollisionResistant) protection against string hash-flooding DoS attacks on .NET Framework.

In the same eager diagnostic ternary modified on line 1077, the derivedKeyAttribute branch still calls derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() without null propagation. If a closed generic value type in a referenced assembly has a member annotated with an attribute derived from KeyAttribute, GetSyntax returns null for metadata and throws NullReferenceException in both the generator and the analyzer.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts the syntax node using 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax'. For positional record or record-struct properties declared in source in the current compilation (e.g. '[property: Key(null)] string Key'), DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax() is a ParameterSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null (Location.None) and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (line 1446) silently drops the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic even in the defining project.

Both MsgPack004.md (line 52) and README.md (line 1642) tell users that member problems on types from referenced assemblies are reported by the defining project, which does not hold when the defining assembly only references MessagePack.Annotations without MessagePack.SourceGenerator; in that common contract-assembly setup neither compilation reports MsgPack004 and unkeyed members are silently skipped.
